title: Website Accessibility Basics for Small Businesses

cover.alt: Concept illustration of keyboard navigation connecting readable, labeled website controls on an inclusive design workbench.

figures.title: Four principles behind an accessible page
figures.summary: The article organizes accessibility around how people perceive, use, and understand content.

items.label: Perceivable
items.detail: Provide text alternatives, captions, and sufficient contrast.

items.label: Operable
items.detail: Make controls work by keyboard without trapping focus.

items.label: Understandable
items.detail: Use clear language, predictable navigation, and useful form guidance.

items.label: Robust
items.detail: Use appropriate HTML and assistive-technology-compatible structure.

figures.caption: The POUR framework described in this article, summarized without making a legal compliance determination.

figures.title: Three practical ways to test the experience
figures.summary: Combine hands-on checks rather than relying on a single automated score.

items.label: Keyboard path
items.detail: Try Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, and relevant arrow-key controls.

items.label: Screen reader pass
items.detail: Check whether headings, labels, and controls communicate their purpose.

items.label: Contrast review
items.detail: Measure text and background combinations with a contrast checker.

items.label: Automated scan
items.detail: Use axe or WAVE to identify additional structural issues for review.

figures.caption: The article's testing methods work together; an automated pass alone does not establish full accessibility.
